correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the deletion–reattachment bijection for marked leaves and the classical complete multipartite spanning-tree count. For every proper marked set, each deleted vertex in V_i has precisely n-n_i-|S|+s_i allowed connections to remaining vertices; multiplying attachment counts and residual tree number gives the exact factorization including all zero/one-remaining-vertex boundaries. Each positive factor log(n-|S|) or log(n-n_i-|S outside V_i|) is concave in a modular cardinality; nonnegative exponents yield lattice submodularity, and r-2>0 yields strict incomparable inequality in r>=3. For r=2 factorization between S_A,S_B proves all mixed Bernoulli moments factor and thus vector independence via inclusion-exclusion. Independent Prüfer enumeration of six multipartite profiles of orders 3–5 confirmed all exact subset moments and all 1920 ordered lattice comparisons. The finite checks corroborate, not establish, the all-size inequality.

final_claim: For uniform labeled spanning tree of K_(n1,...,nr), n>=3, r>=2, probability that every vertex in S is a leaf equals ((n-|S|)/n)^(r-2)*product_i(1-(|S|-s_i)/(n-n_i))^(n_i-1) for proper S, and is 0 for whole vertex set. For all A,B it is log-submodular on the set lattice, strictly so for incomparable A,B with positive RHS when r>=3; for r=2 the entire leaf-indicator vectors in different parts are independent; for r>=3 all distinct single leaf indicators have strictly negative covariance.
